page: Microsoft Azure E128-64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile is built around an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The instance is characterized by a constrained CPU-to-memory ratio, pairing 64 active vCPUs with 1024.0 GB of system memory, which allocates 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features bundled local storage comprising 7560 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, avoiding network-attached storage latency for local data operations. No discrete graphical processing units (GPUs) are provisioned on this instance type.

Benchmark results validate strong compute and memory subsystem performance. The AMD EPYC processor scores in the top tier (top 10%) on Geekbench single-core (2891.0) and multi-core (26776.0), as well as PassMark CPU score (94640.85). Large-block uncached memory read throughput reaches 206.52 GB/sec and write throughput records 133.04 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Local operational workloads show high execution capacity, reaching 37846.03 on PassMark database operations and 101.98 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks.

This server trades compute density for memory and local I/O capacity, constraining vCPUs relative to the underlying 128-vCPU chassis to minimize memory-bound resource contention. It is suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, enterprise database management systems, data processing pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs on 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 1024.0 GB of system memory (16.0 GB per vCPU) and bundles 7560 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPUs. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. Benchmark results highlight top-tier performance across Geekbench multi-core (26776.0), PassMark CPU execution (94640.85), and database processing metrics (37846.03), along with an uncached memory read bandwidth of 206.52 GB/sec. This configuration offers high memory density relative to core count, making it well suited for enterprise database management systems, high-capacity in-memory data stores, large-scale caching layers, and high-throughput data processing pipelines requiring extensive local NVMe scratch storage.
